problem_text:
A retail distribution center must devise a procurement and stock management strategy for a critical electronic component over a forthcoming 12-week interval.  
The initial stock level at the commencement of the planning window is 32 items.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 12 \), the manufacturer permits the center to submit a purchase request whose size must fall between 8 and 53 items.  
Nevertheless, every procurement request that is submitted will require a lead time of 3 weeks before it becomes available for fulfilling requirements or rebuilding stock.  
The requirement for the component in each week is provided as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 32 items  
* Week 2: requirement 47 items  
* Week 3: requirement 15 items  
* Week 4: requirement 15 items  
* Week 5: requirement 45 items  
* Week 6: requirement 21 items  
* Week 7: requirement 26 items  
* Week 8: requirement 22 items  
* Week 9: requirement 26 items  
* Week 10: requirement 30 items  
* Week 11: requirement 54 items  
* Week 12: requirement 55 items  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning interval, component amounts may be expressed as fractions, and the aggregate volume of physical stock present at any moment must not surpass the storage limit of 32 items.  
The aggregate expense across the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 2 per item ordered; the storage expense, which amounts to 2 per item of stock retained from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, which amounts to 14 per item of unfulfilled requirement. Determine the optimal purchase quantity for each week and monitor the consequent stock and shortage quantities so as to minimize the total expense.
